leak: Every 'sharp money' reading on this board - the line-movement arrows, the CONFIRMED and FADE tags, the veto that blocked plays when professionals moved against us, and the finding that 'sharps lost their edge at the trade deadline' - was measured against opening lines that had no date attached and were never replaced. Teams play three and four game series: the 'opening line' for most games was actually a PREVIOUS game's line, sometimes months old. 615 of 619 sharp signals ever recorded were comparing prices from two different games.
ev: The owner called it: sharps don't lose their edge - that's what makes them sharp. Re-measured with a clean ruler (each morning's real price against the true pre-pitch close), the side the market moved toward won 51% before the deadline and 48% after - a coin flip in both eras. The dramatic 56.6%-to-53.5% 'decay' was cross-game price differences masquerading as sharp action. The veto's founding evidence (2-15 in paper trading) was built on the same broken ruler.
fix: Opening lines are now saved per date, movement is only ever computed inside a single game's own day, and the sharp-fade veto no longer blocks anything - the signal is still computed and logged on clean data, but it earns its way back in from zero evidence or it stays decorative. What the clean data DID reveal: the model's own closing-line edge genuinely decayed after the deadline (+1.44% and 69% beat before, -0.73% and 51% after) - hidden until now behind the frozen tile. That number is the real deadline story, it is now live on the board nightly, and it is the one being watched.

leak: The July 29 fix for fake closing lines had a side effect nobody noticed: by grading time each night, the odds feed has already dropped that day's finished games, so the date filter correctly rejected tomorrow's lines and then found nothing at all. Every closing-line comparison since July 29 was silently recorded as empty - while the site kept displaying the last healthy numbers as if they were current.
ev: Caught by the owner, who noticed the 69% close-beat figure hadn't moved in a month. Sure enough: 336 empty entries since July 29, and a stat tile still hardcoded to numbers from July. Rebuilt against true pre-pitch price snapshots, the honest figures are lower: plays beat the final price 61% of the time at +0.5% average (not 69% at +3.5%), and over just the repaired month the plays actually ran slightly behind the close (54% beat, -0.6%).
fix: Three-part fix. Closing prices are now captured an hour BEFORE each first pitch, while the game still exists on the feed, and the grader reads those. The missing month was rebuilt from historical pre-pitch snapshots. And the stat tile now computes from the live log every night instead of a number typed in once. The sharper standard cuts both ways: the model's close-beating edge is thinner than displayed, and that is now the number on the board - which matters, because beating the close is half of the new report card.

leak: Every part of the system identified a game as 'Away@Home'. A doubleheader puts two games on that one name, so game 2's starters, prices and flag silently overwrote game 1's - the site showed the same matchup twice with identical data, and the nightly grader would have scored the game-2 play against game 1's final score.
ev: Caught live by a subscriber on the Cardinals-Reds twin bill. The 9:00 AM lineup lock texted a Cardinals play for GAME 1 (10:40 AM) - but the text carried game 2's starters and price, and the site showed both games as the same -116 official play. Subscribers bet game 1; the Cardinals won 2-1. During the repair the not-yet-played game 2 briefly graded as a WIN off game 1's final, and a stray 'no bet, game already started' note went out for the finished game 1 - both symptoms of one name covering two games.
fix: Games now carry their MLB game ID and game number end to end. Doubleheader game 2 gets its own key everywhere (lineups, prices, plays, texts, the paper F5 ledger, the board), and any row that knows its game ID grades ONLY against that game - no fallback that a twin's score could leak through. The record: game 1 IS the texted play (win, at the texted -116); game 2 was never texted and is not a play. Subscribers were sent a clarification.

leak: Plays were firing in matchups where a starting pitcher had almost no season data, forcing the model to lean on career stats.
ev: Bets trusting OUR OWN thin-sample starter: 11-22, -$759. Bets fading a thin starter: 16-13, +$269. Thin starters with elite swing-and-miss (11%+ whiff): their teams win 55% - the market knows the returning ace better than a career-stat blend does.
fix: Side-aware gate: the starter behind our bet needs ~50+ innings; thin opponents are fadeable only when their stuff is unproven. We fade call-ups, never returning aces.

leak: CLV was graded against 'closing' odds pulled at 10:30 PM - which, for finished games, could be the NEXT day's lines for the same teams.
ev: Rebuilt against true pre-pitch snapshots (545 games): the flattering +2.65% average CLV was really +0.77% on all picks. But flagged plays held up: +6.49%, beating the true close 96% of the time.
fix: Every graded game re-scored against the actual line 10 minutes before its first pitch; closing lines now date-filtered permanently.

leak: The odds feed returns several days of games. Prices were keyed by team name only, so tomorrow's line could silently overwrite today's - producing phantom edges and wrong prices in alerts.
ev: Caught live: one game showed a 90-cent spread across books (two different games mixed); one play fired on next-day prices and would not have qualified at the real ones.
fix: Every price consumer filters to the exact slate date before reading a single number.

leak: A play could be texted at 2 PM, then a later pre-game re-run would re-price the game and silently drop or change the flag - so the record graded something different than what subscribers bet.
ev: Caught when a texted -105 play vanished from the nightly grade; the day was reported 1-1 when the truth was 1-2.
fix: Lock-on-text: the moment a play is texted, its price and flag are frozen. The texted price IS the official play, forever.

leak: When the value was on the underdog, the graders scored the bet as if it were on the favorite - value-dog wins were recorded as losses for months.
ev: 13 bets graded on the wrong team. Corrected season P&L swung from -$1,425 to -$152 - over $1,200 of losses never happened.
fix: One shared source of truth for which side carries every bet, used by every grader, notifier, and report. Covered by regression tests.

leak: The old pipeline bet its biggest edges hardest - and they were its worst bets.
ev: Edges of 10%+ claimed 58.9% confidence and cashed 44.6%. The 3-6% zone claimed 52.7% and cashed 61.8%. Moderate disagreement with the market is signal; huge disagreement is usually our error.
fix: The 3-8% bet window: bets live where the model has been right, capped before the zone where the market is.

leak: On every game with confirmed lineups, the old inference code fed each team's offense into the model under the OTHER team's label - flipping the sign of the second-strongest feature.
ev: Re-scoring 117 live games: the raw model picked at 58.1% while the full buggy pipeline delivered 53.9%.
fix: V2 rebuilt with one shared feature module for training and inference - the same definition, mathematically incapable of drifting apart.

leak: After the model produced a calibrated probability, four hand-tuned adjustments (park factor, home boost, bullpen nudge, probability clamp) 'improved' it.
ev: The layers flipped 28% of picks; the raw model won 57.6% of those disagreements. The clamp alone discarded the model's most confident - and most accurate - calls.
fix: All four layers deleted. Park and bullpen numbers are still shown as context; they just don't touch the number.

leak: The weekly retrain silently excluded the current season from training - 757 of the freshest games taught the model nothing, all season.
ev: The 'current season weighted 3x' log line printed every week; the rows it referenced were never in the training set.
fix: Trains on everything, validated by walk-forward so no holdout season is needed for an honest number.

leak: The old model used 18 inputs. Permutation testing showed 13 of them made out-of-sample predictions WORSE - extra dimensions the model used to memorize the past.
ev: Only the pitching gap carried clearly positive signal. Walk-forward: the 4-feature rebuild beat the 18-feature original 60.2% to 58.7%.
fix: Four winsorized features into a calibrated logistic regression. Any new feature must beat this baseline out-of-sample before earning a slot - tested, never assumed.

leak: The old pipeline kept betting into games where professional money had moved the line against it.
ev: Those bets went 2-15 (13.3%) for -$1,062 before the veto existed. Sharps opposing the model win ~58% of the time.
fix: The FADE veto: any play with significant sharp movement against it is killed automatically, no exceptions.

leak: The closing-line tracker silently stopped capturing closes at the end of July - the odds API drops finished games - and the board's CLV tile was a hardcoded number that could never change.
ev: The tile read +6.49% / 96% beat for a month straight. The owner noticed it had not moved and asked. He was right.
fix: True closes are now captured about an hour before every first pitch, 334 historical games were re-scored from archived snapshots, and the tile is computed live from the log every night. The UPDATED stamp now shows the DATA's timestamp, not the browser clock.

leak: Opening lines were saved without a date and never overwritten, so in any series the 'sharp money' signal compared today's game against a PREVIOUS game's line.
ev: 615 of 619 sharp-movement signals were measured against the wrong game. The FADE veto's famous 2-15 evidence was built on this. The owner called it: sharps don't lose their edge.
fix: Openings are date-scoped (and doubleheader-scoped) per game. The sharp veto is retired from live play until a clean signal earns its way back; the movement is still logged for study.

leak: The graders trusted the picks files' bet flags instead of the record of what was actually texted, so a flag that never became a play could count in the official record.
ev: One July 21 game carried a bet flag in the file that was never sent to anyone. It sat inside the official record for five weeks. A weekend of untexted flags was heading the same way.
fix: Every grader now cross-checks the sent-text log before counting anything - lock-on-text is enforced by code across the record, the weekly report, the analytics, and this site. The phantom is gone from the record.

leak: Doubleheaders shared one key almost everywhere - picks, opening lines, first-five grading, closing-line attribution, player cards - so game 2 could silently overwrite or mis-grade game 1.
ev: The Aug 17 Cardinals-Reds twin bill collided live on this site: the 9 AM texted play and the afternoon game showed as one game. Subscribers took the morning game; the record briefly graded the wrong one.
fix: Every pipeline now keys game 1 and game 2 separately, end to end. Closing-line entries that cannot be attributed to a specific game of a twin bill are excluded rather than guessed.

leak: Closing prices were only recorded for the model's PICK side - but most plays bet the other side (the value dog), so the close of the side we actually bet was never captured.
ev: 29 of 75 plays had no true bet-side close. Estimating the missing half from a margin assumption flips the verdict from 56% beat to 39% beat - the assumption WAS the answer.
fix: Both sides' true closes are recorded on every play from Aug 27 on. The board only publishes the measured plays (41% beat on 46 plays - negative, and printed anyway) and refuses to estimate the rest.

leak: The props boards' morning predictions could be silently rebuilt later in the day - after lineups, even after games started - which would let a bad morning call vanish.
ev: Caught by code review before it was caught rewriting history: reruns of the model scripts on a started slate would regenerate the frozen logs in place.
fix: Frozen means frozen: the HR, hits, and strikeout models now refuse by code to rebuild a log once the slate has started, and refuse past dates entirely. The graded ledgers only ever see the morning's frozen predictions.

leak: The props ledger's 'top picks' tables were built from players who RECORDED a stat line, so a top pick who was scratched or benched quietly fell out of his own report card.
ev: Survivorship bias in miniature: the exact mechanism that makes bad funds look good. Also: two players named Max Muncy shared one row.
fix: Top-pick tables are now selected from the full morning list including did-not-plays, and every player table is keyed by league ID, not name.

leak: For traded pitchers, the weekly training pipeline read only the newest team's partial-season stats - a three-start stint could stand in for a full season in the model's training data.
ev: Deadline season is exactly when this bites hardest, and this audit began as a deadline investigation. The live pick engine had the fix; the training side did not - they were learning from different books.
fix: Training now uses combined full-season totals for traded players, matching the live engine. A visible warning fires whenever a pitcher's stats fall back to a weaker source, instead of silently gating him at 0% reliability.
